modules.title: Pronunciation Clarity
modules.reason: Improve how clearly individual words and sounds are produced.
modules.checkpoint: Complete the exercises and produce three clearly understandable speaking attempts.

items.title: Pronunciation Exercise 1
items.description: Watch, imitate, then repeat the exercise.

items.title: Pronunciation Exercise 2
items.description: Watch, repeat, record yourself and compare.

items.title: Record 3 clear speaking attempts
items.description: Use Read Aloud or another assigned speaking question and focus on clarity.

modules.title: Pronunciation — Word Endings
modules.reason: Make final consonants, plural endings and -ed endings audible.
modules.checkpoint: Produce the target endings clearly in at least 8 out of 10 items.

items.title: Target ending drill
items.description: Practise 10 target words, then use them in 10 short sentences.

items.title: Apply endings in PTE speaking
items.description: Complete the teacher-assigned speaking questions without dropping final sounds.

modules.title: Pronunciation — Problem Sounds
modules.reason: Work on the specific consonant or vowel contrast that is reducing clarity.
modules.checkpoint: Produce the target sound clearly in at least 8 out of 10 items.

items.title: Minimal-pair practice
items.description: Practise the exact sound pair identified by your teacher.

items.title: Sentence application
items.description: Use the target sound in short sentences and record yourself.

modules.title: Fluency — Chunking
modules.reason: Develop smoother phrasing by speaking in meaningful groups of words.
modules.checkpoint: Produce three smooth recordings with sensible chunking.

items.title: Chunk-marking drill
items.description: Mark meaningful chunks in 5 short passages before speaking.

items.title: Shadow and record
items.description: Shadow a model, then record the same material without the model.

modules.title: Fluency — Pauses & Recovery
modules.reason: Keep speaking after small errors instead of stopping and restarting.
modules.checkpoint: Complete three timed attempts without disruptive pauses.

items.title: 30–60 second response drills
items.description: Practise continuing smoothly even when you make a small mistake.

modules.title: Fluency — Pace
modules.reason: Maintain a steady pace without rushing or slowing excessively.
modules.checkpoint: Maintain a steady, understandable pace in three recordings.

items.title: Controlled pace recording
items.description: Record the same response three times at a steady pace.

modules.title: Content Picking — Main Idea
modules.reason: Identify the central idea before adding supporting information.
modules.checkpoint: Identify the correct central idea in at least 4 out of 5 attempts.

items.title: Main idea drill
items.description: For 5 passages or audios, identify only the central idea before writing or speaking.

modules.title: Content Picking — Prioritisation
modules.reason: Separate essential information from examples and minor details.
modules.checkpoint: Select concise, relevant information in at least 4 out of 5 attempts.

items.title: Essential vs minor detail
items.description: Reduce each source to 3–4 essential points and remove examples.

modules.title: SWT — Context Accuracy
modules.reason: Preserve the original relationship between ideas, including cause, contrast and viewpoint.
modules.checkpoint: Produce at least 4 out of 5 summaries without changing the source meaning.

items.title: Source vs summary check
items.description: Compare each sentence with the source and highlight any changed relationship or contradiction.

modules.title: Describe Image — Content Picking
modules.reason: Choose the most reportable features instead of trying to describe everything.
modules.checkpoint: Identify the topic and 3–4 important features in at least 4 out of 5 images within preparation time.

items.title: Content-only image drill
items.description: Do not speak yet. Identify topic, overall pattern, biggest/smallest and meaningful comparisons.

modules.title: Note-Taking — Keywords
modules.reason: Capture useful content words without writing full sentences.
modules.checkpoint: Capture the main idea and important support without falling behind.

items.title: Keyword-only notes
items.description: Use 5 short audios and write only content words and symbols.

modules.title: SGD — Speaker Tracking
modules.reason: Track who said what and where speakers agree or disagree.
modules.checkpoint: Track all speakers correctly in at least 4 out of 5 discussions.

items.title: S1 / S2 / S3 note grid
items.description: Record each speaker's key viewpoint in a separate column.

modules.title: Note-Taking — Speed
modules.reason: Use abbreviations and symbols so notes do not fall behind the audio.
modules.checkpoint: Capture the main idea and support while keeping pace with the audio.

items.title: 30–60 second note-speed drills
items.description: Use abbreviations, arrows and content words only.

modules.title: Grammar — Sentence Building
modules.reason: Connect important ideas accurately using controlled clauses.
modules.checkpoint: Produce at least 4 out of 5 structurally accurate sentences.

items.title: Sentence-combining drill
items.description: Combine 2–3 related ideas while preserving meaning.

modules.title: Grammar — Run-ons & Punctuation
modules.reason: Control long sentences and clause boundaries.
modules.checkpoint: Produce at least 4 out of 5 controlled sentences without run-ons.

items.title: Run-on repair
items.description: Repair 10 long sentences, then apply the same control to your PTE response.

modules.title: Vocabulary — Collocations
modules.reason: Learn common word combinations rather than isolated vocabulary.
modules.checkpoint: Reach at least 80% across three practice sets.

items.title: Collocation notebook
items.description: Record the full phrase, meaning and one example sentence.

items.title: Context practice
items.description: Complete the teacher-assigned Fill in the Blanks questions.

modules.title: Comprehension — Distractors
modules.reason: Use evidence to separate the best answer from plausible distractors.
modules.checkpoint: Answer at least 4 out of 5 questions correctly and explain the evidence.

items.title: Evidence drill
items.description: For each option, identify why it is supported or why it should be rejected.

modules.title: Spelling — Personal Error Log
modules.reason: Target the spelling mistakes you personally repeat.
modules.checkpoint: Reach at least 90% on your personal error list twice.

items.title: Build your error list
items.description: Record every repeated spelling error with the corrected form.

items.title: Retest
items.description: Retest the same words after 2–3 days.

modules.title: Listening Memory — Chunking
modules.reason: Retain meaning and word groups instead of trying to memorise isolated words.
modules.checkpoint: Substantially retain at least 4 out of 5 sentences.

items.title: Memory ladder
items.description: Start with short chunks and gradually increase sentence length.

modules.title: Listening Memory — Word Order
modules.reason: Retain sentence order, articles, prepositions and other small words.
modules.checkpoint: Retain order and key function words in at least 4 out of 5 sentences.

items.title: Reconstruction drill
items.description: Rebuild short sentences from chunks, then progress to longer dictation.

modules.title: RTS — Register & Functional Language
modules.reason: Match your language to the audience, purpose and desired outcome.
modules.checkpoint: Produce appropriate responses in at least 4 out of 5 situations.

items.title: Respond to a Situation — Exercise 1
items.description: Watch how the response identifies the audience, purpose and appropriate wording.

items.title: Respond to a Situation — Exercise 2
items.description: Watch, then apply the same audience-and-purpose thinking to a new situation.

items.title: Audience and purpose drill
items.description: Identify who you are speaking to, why, and what outcome you need before responding.

modules.title: SWT Content Selection — Highlight Trainer
modules.reason: Practise deciding what belongs in the summary before worrying about sentence writing.
modules.checkpoint: Complete at least 10 existing-passage selection exercises and review every missed central idea.

items.title: Highlight the important lines — 15 exercises
items.description: Use existing SWT passages. Highlight only the sentences that carry the central message or essential support. After each submission, the trainer shows what you missed, why it matters, and the central key phrases/sentences. No full summary writing.

modules.title: SWT — How to Attempt & Form
modules.reason: Learn the complete SWT method. If your difficulty is choosing important lines or ideas, use SWT Content Selection — Highlight Trainer first.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 4 out of 5 SWT responses with relevant content, valid one-sentence form and controlled language.

items.title: Know what is scored
items.description: Check your response against Content (4), Form (1), Grammar (2) and Vocabulary (2).

items.title: Pick the central message first
items.description: If content selection is difficult, use the dedicated Highlight Trainer rather than manually ticking this step.

items.title: Write one controlled sentence
items.description: Connect the selected ideas logically in one sentence of 5–75 words without changing the original meaning.

modules.title: Timing & Preparation
modules.reason: Apply a known strategy reliably within PTE timing.
modules.checkpoint: Complete at least 4 out of 5 attempts within the required timing.

items.title: Three-stage timing
items.description: Practise untimed, then with reduced preparation time, then under full test conditions.

modules.title: SST — How to Attempt
modules.reason: Use an efficient listening, note-taking and summary method while meeting the task's scoring requirements.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 4 out of 5 SST attempts with relevant content, correct form and controlled language.

items.title: How to Attempt Summarise Spoken Text
items.description: Watch the task method before practising.

items.title: Topic + key-point notes
items.description: Listen for the topic and the strongest supporting points; use keywords rather than full sentences in your notes.

items.title: Write a connected SST summary
items.description: Turn the notes into a clear 50–70 word response, then check Content, Form, Grammar, Vocabulary and Spelling.

modules.title: Essay Writing — Core Method
modules.reason: Understand the prompt, plan a clear response, develop relevant ideas and meet the essay scoring requirements.
modules.checkpoint: Complete an essay that addresses the prompt, meets form requirements and shows clear development and organisation.

items.title: Identify the question type and requirements
items.description: Underline what the prompt asks you to discuss, compare, explain or give an opinion on. Give an opinion only when the prompt requires it.

items.title: Plan before writing
items.description: Prepare a clear position where needed, two body ideas and relevant supporting explanation/examples.

items.title: Write and review against the score traits
items.description: Check Content, Form, Grammar, Vocabulary, Spelling, General Linguistic Range, and Development/Structure/Coherence.
